hitom.source: Yinghui He, Yufan Wu, Yilin Jia, Rada Mihalcea, Yulong Chen, Naihao Deng (2023). Hi-ToM: A Benchmark for Evaluating Higher-Order Theory of Mind Reasoning in Large Language Models. In Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023. arXiv:2310.16755. https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.16755 ; GitHub: https://github.com/ying-hui-he/Hi-ToM_dataset
hitom.notes_specific: Table 5 (the paper's only proper numeric table, p.6) reports OVERALL accuracy (collapsed across ToM order 0-4) by model x prompting(VP/CoTP) x deception(w/,w/o). It does NOT break accuracy down by ToM order. The only order-by-order (0-4) accuracy numbers in the paper are the printed cell labels in Figures 10-13 (Appendix C.2, 'Standard accuracy results'), which are heatmaps further stratified by story length (1-3 chapters) and deception status -- the paper does not report an order-only marginal accuracy (that would require averaging cells ourselves, which we did NOT do to avoid inferring/estimating a value the paper itself never states). The 'results' array above transcribes every cell from Figures 10-13 exactly as printed, so users can compute their own order-marginal average if desired. GPT-4 additionally has JOINT accuracy (stricter metric requiring all lower orders also correct) reported in Figure 3 (GPT-4, GPT-3.5) and Figures 8-9 (Claude, Guanaco); we did not transcribe joint accuracy since the user asked for accuracy by order, and standard accuracy (Figures 10-13) is the more directly comparable metric.
hitom.order_marginal_derived_note: Computed by us (not stated as a single number in the paper): mean of the per-cell accuracies in hitom.results, averaged across story_length_chapters (1,2,3) and deception (with/without) for each (model, prompting, order). Source cells are Figures 10-13 of arXiv:2310.16755.

fantom.notes_specific: Order breakdown (first-order vs second-order, cyclic/acyclic) comes ONLY from Table 4 (p.8), which reports BeliefQ[Choice] accuracy. Table 4's caption/surrounding text does not explicitly state whether it uses the short or full conversation context; every other table/figure in that same results subsection (Figs 2-3, Tables 1-3) is explicitly stated to use the SHORT context, and full-conversation numbers are reported separately and only in Table 9 (which has no order breakdown). We flag Table 4's context as unconfirmed rather than asserting 'short'. ALL* is the paper's headline metric (Table 9 col 1): fraction of question SETS where the model answers ALL SIX ToM question types correctly for the same info piece (strictest metric). ALL (col 2) is the same but excluding BeliefQ[Dist.] (used for human comparison since humans were not given BeliefQ[Dist.], AnswerabilityQ[Y/N], or InfoAccessQ[Y/N] -- confirmed via Table 1/Figure 2 cross-check: Human ALL=87.5, BeliefQ[Choice]=93.8, AnswerabilityQ[List]=InfoAccessQ[List]=90.6, all other Human cells blank in Table 9). IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the request: the paper does NOT report F1 for the list-type questions (AnswerabilityQ[List], InfoAccessQ[List] are scored as plain accuracy, all-or-nothing). F1 is reported only for: (a) BeliefQ[Dist.] and FactQ, as token-overlap F1 against free-form responses, and (b) AnswerabilityQ[Y/N] and InfoAccessQ[Y/N], as weighted F1 over yes/no responses. These are included above with explicit metric labels.

notes:
GENERAL: All numbers above were transcribed directly from the arXiv PDFs (arXiv:2310.16755 for Hi-ToM, arXiv:2310.15421v3 for FANToM), extracted with PyMuPDF and cross-checked against an independent HTML (ar5iv/arxiv-html) extraction pass where possible. None of the values are computed, averaged, or estimated by us except where explicitly marked. 

HI-TOM SPECIFICS: (1) Table 5 gives OVERALL accuracy per model x prompting(VP='no-CoT'/CoTP='CoT') x deception, NOT broken down by ToM order -- this is the only clean 'table' the paper provides. (2) Order-by-order (0-4) accuracy exists only as printed cell labels in heatmap Figures 10-13 (Appendix C.2), which are additionally split by story length (1-3 chapters) and deception status; we transcribed every cell rather than averaging across story length/deception, since the paper itself never reports a pure order-marginal number -- averaging would have been an inference on our part, which we were told to avoid. If you need a single order-only number, you would need to average the 'results' entries yourself (and decide how to weight story lengths, which the paper does not specify). (3) A stricter 'joint accuracy' metric (Figure 3 for GPT-4/GPT-3.5, Figures 8-9 for Claude/Guanaco) also exists in the paper but was NOT transcribed here since the user asked for standard accuracy by order. (4) We did not find a public results.md/leaderboard file in the Hi-ToM GitHub repo beyond what's in the paper -- 'not found' for any additional models/numbers beyond the four in the paper (GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4-32k, Claude-instant, Guanaco 65B).

FANTOM SPECIFICS: (1) Order breakdown (Table 4) does not explicitly state short vs. full input -- see fantom.notes_specific above; treat as 'likely short, unconfirmed' rather than verified. (2) The request asked for F1 on list-type questions; the paper reports ACCURACY (not F1) for AnswerabilityQ[List] and InfoAccessQ[List] -- F1 is reported only for the Y/N and free-form (Dist./FactQ) question types. This is a correction, not a 'not found'. (3) ALL* is reported in Table 9 for every model/CoT/FT variant and both short and full conversation contexts (see fantom.table9_full_results, metric='ALL*'). (4) Human performance was only measured for BeliefQ[Choice], AnswerabilityQ[List], and InfoAccessQ[List] under the SHORT context (Human ALL=87.5%); Human was not evaluated on BeliefQ[Dist.], AnswerabilityQ[Y/N], InfoAccessQ[Y/N], FactQ, ALL*, or the FULL conversation context at all -- those cells are 'not found' because the paper does not report them (not because we failed to locate them). (5) We did not check the FANToM GitHub repo's README for a leaderboard beyond the paper; the paper's Table 9 was already comprehensive enough to cover all 13+ evaluated models.
